title: FTP Control settings and API object

prose.text: {{allow-fohttp}} {{native-ftp-scoping}} {{urls-need-proxy-retrieval}} {{allowed-urls-count-toward-custom-limit}} {{console-has-no-action-or-user-scope}} The ALLOW, CAUTION and BLOCK actions belong to File Type Control: [[zia.file-type-control.actions]].
Over the API: {{api-get-put}} {{api-fields}} {{enable-fohttp-flag}} The shape of `urlCategories` differs between sources {{divergence:url-categories-element-type}}.
The default of the native FTP switch is open {{gap:native-ftp-default}}, and how Allow Any URL Category appears in the API is open {{gap:allow-any-category-representation}}.
Defaults and passive-only behavior are in [[zia.firewall]]; who the policy applies to is in [[zia.ftp-control.scope]].

checks.do: Whether a rule list, action column or user scoping is being sought for FTP, since the console documents none.
Whether URL Filtering precedence explains an FTP failure, checked before the user's location when the settings look right.

allow-fohttp.statement: The FTP Control page has an Allow FTP over HTTP option that lets browsers connect to FTP over HTTP sites and download files. A remote user on a dedicated port is supported for FTP over HTTP.

quotes: Enable this option to allow browsers to connect to FTP over HTTP sites and download files.
If a remote user uses a dedicated port, then the service supports FTP over HTTP for them.

native-ftp-scoping.statement: Allow Native FTP lets users connect to native FTP sites and download files. When it is on, Allow Any URL Category opens FTP to every category. With that off, the policy is limited to the Allowed URL Categories (super categories, categories or both, including custom categories) and up to 25,000 Allowed URLs.

quotes: Allow Native FTP: Enable this option to allow users to connect to native FTP sites and download files.
Allow Any URL Category: Enable this option to allow FTP traffic for all URL categories.
Allowed URL Categories: You can select URL super categories, URL categories, or both.
You can also search for categories or add a custom category by clicking the Add icon.
You can add up to 25,000 URLs.

urls-need-proxy-retrieval.statement: Allowed URLs work when the FTP proxy can retrieve the URLs. With transparent traffic forwarding, enter an IP address instead of a URL. The vendor's alternatives are an FQDN-based Firewall rule that allows the traffic, forward proxy mode, or FTP traffic over HTTP CONNECT.

quotes: This feature is successful when the FTP proxy can retrieve the URLs.
If you are using transparent traffic forwarding, enter an IP address instead of a URL.
Alternatively, Zscaler recommends implementing one of the following workarounds:
FQDN-based Firewall rule set to allow traffic

allowed-urls-count-toward-custom-limit.statement: Allowed URLs in FTP Control settings count toward the 25K custom URLs/TLDs limit, together with custom category entries, auth exemption URLs and the other lists the limits page names.

quotes: Custom URLs/TLDs | 25K URLs/TLDs | Includes:Custom URLs/TLDs in all URL Categories/TLD CategoriesAuth Exemption URLs in Advanced settingsBlocked Malicious URLs in Advanced Threat Protection settingsBlocked URLs in SSL Inspection settingsAllowed URLs in FTP Control settingsBandwidth Class Domains
The default limit for custom URLs/TLDs is 25K.

console-has-no-action-or-user-scope.statement: The FTP Control configuration steps describe two allow-or-block settings, FTP over HTTP and native FTP, with URL category and URL scoping for native FTP. They describe no allow/block/alert action selector and no user, group or department scoping.

quotes: Allow or block FTP over HTTP traffic and native FTP traffic.
You can also allow or block native FTP traffic by URL categories or specified URLs.

console-has-no-action-or-user-scope.conditions: Rests on an absence. The recaptured configuration page (revision 3240462) lists every setting on the Edit page; none is an action or a user, group, department or location selector. A tenant console could still expose more than the help page documents.

api-get-put.statement: FTP Control is one settings object. The API exposes `GET` and `PUT` on `/ftpSettings` and nothing to create or delete rules.

expect.operationId: Ftp Settings Resource Get Ftp Settings
Ftp Settings Resource Update Ftp Settings

api-get-put.conditions: The 'nothing to create or delete' half rests on the path item holding only `get` and `put` in the contract.

api-fields.statement: The settings object has four fields: `ftpOverHttpEnabled`, `ftpEnabled`, `urlCategories` and `urls`. A read returns `ftpEnabled` and `ftpOverHttpEnabled` always.

enable-fohttp-flag.statement: Enabling FTP over HTTP for Client Connector and PAC users is a single boolean write, `ftpOverHttpEnabled`, scoped by `urlCategories` and `urls`; there is no per-flow rule object.
enable-fohttp-flag.conditions: Follows from the console option, the API fields and the settings object's GET/PUT shape (the claims derived from); the absence of a per-flow rule object rests on the API surface having no FTP rule endpoint.

url-categories-element-type.summary: The contract shapes `urlCategories` as objects; the Python SDK model forms the list as strings.

positions.says: urlCategories items are URL category objects (name, backendName, urlSupercategory and more).

quotes: config["urlCategories"] if "urlCategories" in config else [], str

positions.says: The model forms the urlCategories list with element type str.

url-categories-element-type.impact: Reading or round-tripping `urlCategories` through the Python SDK may not preserve the category objects the API returns. What the API accepts on write is not shown by either source.

native-ftp-default.title: Default of ftpEnabled and what turning it off does
native-ftp-default.detail: The default value of `ftpEnabled` on a new tenant, and what switching it off does to native FTP, is not stated. The FTP over HTTP half is sourced (default-deny, only native FTP allowed by default: zia.firewall:ftp-default). Unverified legacy statement: 'native FTP is default-allow'. The configuration page and the API both carry an Allow Native FTP switch, which the default-allow wording does not explain. Resolves with a tenant read of ftp-control-policy on a fresh tenant or a lab test.
native-ftp-default.blocks: advising whether a tenant that never touched FTP Control allows native FTP

allow-any-category-representation.title: How Allow Any URL Category appears in the API
allow-any-category-representation.detail: The console has an Allow Any URL Category switch for native FTP. The `/ftpSettings` object has no field of that name, only `urlCategories` and `urls`. How 'any category' is represented (an empty list, a specific category, or ignored) is not stated by the contract or the SDK.
allow-any-category-representation.blocks: reading a tenant's native FTP scope from its API object
